collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults who are builders or working)

collection.description: A builder gives a villager two pieces of advice about a new hut: take both, or take only the first.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is building a new hut. (friend), who has built a lot of huts, gives (subject.him/her) two pieces of advice: use thicker poles, and make the roof lower so the wind can't get under it. (subject) likes the first idea. (subject.He/she) does not like the second. (subject.He/she) wants a tall roof (subject.he/she) can stand up in without ducking.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) uses thick poles and builds the roof tall. It's a fine hut and (subject.he/she) can stand up straight in it. In the first big storm it creaks alarmingly, but it holds. "Bit tall," says (friend), looking at it afterwards. "Bit tall," agrees (subject), happily, standing up in it.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) uses thicker poles and a lower roof. The hut is very sturdy. (subject) bangs (subject.his/her) head on the beam every single morning for the first month. (subject.He/she) never says anything to (friend). (subject.He/she) just rubs (subject.his/her) head a lot. Eventually (subject.he/she) learns to duck.
